title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of adding automated sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics using the declared/requested model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks drawn from a deterministic intent_configuration_repair_v1 task bank. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call accounting recorded model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results fall well below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, an artifact-grounded explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, a concise clarification of provider-call accounting under shared_initial_candidate semantics, and reproducibility guidance pointing auditors to the archived execution manifest in the artifact bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational safety requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and higher-order invariants (e.g., make-before-break, keep-one-uplink-up). A common operational pattern is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior system reports and surveys document this workflow-centred mitigation strategy [1]–[3] but provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution when the same initial candidate is shared across conditions.

Research question and contributions. Our preregistered research question was: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and autonomous confirmatory execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete run accounting; (3) a concise exposition and an explicit clarification of provider-call accounting under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (4) an artifact-grounded interpretation of the observed near-zero marginal effect and operational recommendations for when guarded stages are most likely to matter.
sections.related_work: Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Recent surveys and architecturally focused reports document the trend of pairing LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise operational assurance for NetOps artifacts [1]–[3]. Those works emphasize that correctness in intent→configuration pipelines is multidimensional: parser/CLI syntax, command-order/workflow constraints, invariant preservation, and dynamic runtime properties often require different verification primitives. Prototype systems combining generation with verification and execution harnesses report heterogeneous gains—validator-only pipelines catch many errors in curated regimes, while emulation helps expose runtime-only behaviors in other regimes. Motivated by these observations, our paired shared_initial_candidate design isolates only downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation or repair) and avoids confounding from generation variability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistration specified Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440), a minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 for power planning, inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic missingness handling (up to two deterministic reseeds on parser failures), repair limits (≤1 repair model call per task), multiplicity adjustments for exploratory analyses, and contamination controls via deterministic artifact hashing and binary/config version checks.

Task bank, topology templates, and vendor abstractions. Confirmatory items were generated deterministically from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family. The bank covers three abstract vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest contains initial_state, expected_final_state, an explicit natural-language intent, a required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies (e.g., make-before-break). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; in the confirmatory execution there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720.

Model, sampling semantics, and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses); model configuration metadata were archived. The preregistration enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair we obtained a single sampled initial candidate (one provider call) and that identical candidate was used by both downstream conditions (baseline and guarded). This isolates any between-condition discordance to downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation observations or repair) rather than generation variability.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is a deterministic rule-based system that performs: vendor-CLI syntactic parsing and canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break), protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance tests. The validator emits a binary detection flag and a per-episode validator_trace object (validation_before/after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes).

The guarded pipeline applies the baseline validator and then—irrespective of validator outcome—executes the normalized candidate in an automated sandboxed-emulation harness instantiated from the declared topology template. The emulator records runtime observations (interface admin transitions and concurrency, MTU/VLAN application effects, observable reachability consequences) and maps those observations to runtime-observation rules that can trigger guarded detections not covered by the static rule set. The emulation mapping is intentionally conservative: its role is to reveal runtime-only violations not codified as validator rules.

Repair policy and run accounting. The preregistered repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage invocation per task and only after the shared initial candidate was generated and after basiline/emulation observations were available for the guarded condition. Provider-call auditing for the confirmatory execution recorded model_calls_used = 721 with stage_counts showing shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. Because of shared_initial_candidate enforcement, any discordant pair (guarded-only detection) must stem from either an emulation observation that the validator did not encode or from the single recorded repair invocation.

Clarification: provider_call_audit fields and apparent asymmetry. The archived provider-call audit summarizes hosted-model-call events by event type and by association. Key fields are: hosted_model_call_event_count (total model-call events observed), stage_counts (how many calls occurred in each stage, e.g., shared_initial_generation, repair), and condition_counts (a view that maps certain stage calls to the downstream condition with which they are associated). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the dominant provider-call activity is the single shared initial-generation call per pair; those calls are recorded under stage_counts.shared_initial_generation and are reflected in condition_counts under the label "shared" because they serve both downstream conditions. Repair calls—if invoked—are recorded under stage_counts.repair and are attributed to the guarded condition in condition_counts. Hence, condition_counts can show an apparent numerical asymmetry (for this run: "shared": 720, "guarded": 1) even though complete_pair_count = 720 and each pair produced both baseline and guarded condition evaluations. This audit mapping is an accounting convention: the total hosted_model_call_event_count equals the sum of stage_counts (721), and the complete_pair accounting (720 pairs, 1440 episodes across two conditions) is preserved in the deterministic reconciliation artifacts. The convention intentionally distinguishes calls that are materially shared from calls that are condition-specific; it does not imply that one condition lacked evaluation coverage.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inferential outputs (artifact-grounded). The contingency counts were: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values are the direct outputs of the preregistered paired-binary analysis executor and reproduce the archived analysis artifacts.

Discordant-pair attribution and repair accounting. Provider-call auditing and deterministic reconciliation record a single repair-stage invocation (stage_counts: repair = 1) and a unique n10 discordant count. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the permissible causes for that single guarded-only detection are: (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not encoded as a validator violation, or (ii) the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The execution and analysis artifacts together permit an auditor to locate the unique discordant pair_id within the archived execution manifest and inspect the per-episode validator_trace and repair trace to adjudicate which of these alternative mechanisms occurred. The run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair), completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, and failed_episode_count = 0.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative scoring traces show that the vast majority of shared_initial candidates complied with validator rules (validator_violation_count = 0) and that sandboxed emulation largely corroborated validator findings in this curated task bank. Those representative traces illustrate parsed_command_count and required_command_count metrics and the validator version used (deterministic_netops_validator_v5).
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The artifact-grounded evidence supports three primary, non‑exclusive explanations that shape interpretation and operational boundary conditions.

Validator ceiling and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator was intentionally configured to encode the workflow constraints exercised by the curated task bank (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). The baseline marginal success rate of 719/720 (≈99.86%) leaves essentially no headroom for the guarded stage to find additional violations in this constrained regime. In other words, when a validator’s coverage aligns closely with the expected task distribution, a ceiling effect can suppress the observable marginal benefit of runtime emulation.

Curated inclusion and reduced adversarial exposure. Confirmatory items were parser-validated and generated deterministically, which concentrates the sample on tasks the validator can reason about. This reduced the prevalence of adversarial or out-of-distribution inputs where emulation typically discovers runtime-only faults. The absence of irrecoverable parser exclusions confirms the bank’s tight curation.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. By design the same sampled candidate was injected to both conditions; therefore discordance could only arise from downstream guarded-stage observations or from repair activity. The single recorded repair call explains the unique n10 discordant outcome in the run accounting. Different design choices (e.g., permitting independent re-generation in guarded condition) would change the observed marginal contribution by conflating generation and downstream effects.

Operational implications and prescriptions. For operator environments that (a) maintain high-coverage static validators aligned to expected intent patterns, and (b) enforce strict parser-based prevalidation, adding automated sandboxed emulation across all changes is likely to produce few additional detections and may not be cost-effective at scale. By contrast, guarded sandboxing remains valuable in regimes with noisy natural-language intents, broader vendor/CLI diversity, adversarial threat models, or long-lived stateful procedures. Practical approaches we recommend: (i) invest first in validator coverage that encodes high-priority workflow invariants, (ii) deploy guarded sandboxing selectively for high-impact changes or when inputs are uncurated, and (iii) use adversarial/fuzzing test banks to discover validator gaps—seed cases for such fuzzing can be drawn from the archived representative traces.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and a single guarded-only discordant episode. These artifact-grounded findings indicate that, in a regime of tightly curated, parser-validated inputs and a validator closely aligned to task workflows, guarded sandboxing yielded vanishing marginal detection benefit. Whether this conclusion generalizes to adversarial, uncurated, or production-like regimes requires targeted follow-up experiments (expanded vendor diversity, adversarial task banks, and higher-fidelity emulation); the archived execution and representative traces provide reproducible seeds for such extensions.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This study was executed autonomously under the frozen master prompt supplied at autonomy-lock. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). Deterministic validator used: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e. Immutable initial master-prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Human roles and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline autonomously performed literature selection, preregistration, code and prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. No manual human editing of the manuscript technical content occurred after the autonomy lock. The canonical execution manifest and the archived artifact bundle (containing raw results, per-episode traces, analysis artifacts, and reconciliation logs) are archived with the run and serve as the authoritative provenance bundle for independent verification.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across other models and validator designs.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contributions but exclude potential guarded benefits that could arise from independent re-generation or alternative prompting in the guarded condition.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and complex long-lived state transitions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could alter results in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.
Residual provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching are documented as residual uncertainties in the archived reconciliation artifacts despite deterministic audit procedures.
